_comment: Hydrodynamic and manoeuvring constants. These shape how every ship moves; see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. Values are deliberately physical rather than per-class tuning knobs, so that a destroyer handles differently from a battleship because it is smaller and lighter, not because a table says so.

hydrodynamics._comment: Resistance is modelled as R = c * v^2, so power P = R*v = c*v^3. The drag coefficient c is solved per ship from its own design power and design speed, which means no ship needs a hand-authored drag number.
hydrodynamics._surgeAddedMassComment: Water dragged along with the hull when accelerating fore-and-aft. Roughly 5-10% of displacement for a ship-shaped body.
hydrodynamics._bollardThrustComment: Thrust ceiling at zero speed, as a multiple of the resistance at design speed. Prevents the power-limited thrust term (P/v) going singular at rest.
hydrodynamics._asternPowerComment: Astern power available from the reversing turbines, as a fraction of ahead power. 30-45% is typical for WWII steam plant.
hydrodynamics._asternResistanceComment: A hull driven stern-first is not the shape it was designed to be. Resistance rises steeply.
hydrodynamics._maxSternwayComment: Ceiling on sternway as a fraction of design speed. This is NOT derived from power and resistance, and is not pretending to be: astern speed is limited chiefly by propeller thrust breakdown in reverse and by the loads sternway puts on the rudder, neither of which this model simulates. 30% puts Iowa at about 10 knots astern, which matches trials.
hydrodynamics._minimumThrustSpeedComment: m/s. Below this the power-limited thrust term uses this speed instead, to keep P/v finite.

manoeuvring._comment: Turning is driven by rudder angle and forward speed. A ship with no way on cannot steer, which falls out of the v/R term rather than being special-cased.
manoeuvring._tacticalDiameterComment: Steady turning circle diameter at full rudder, in ship lengths. 3.0-4.0 is typical for destroyers, 4.0-5.5 for battleships. Overridden per ship in data/ships/.
manoeuvring._rudderRateComment: How fast the rudder itself moves. Large ships are slower; a damaged steering motor is slower still.
manoeuvring._yawResponseComment: Time constant for the hull to build up to its steady turn rate. Large ships take much longer to answer the helm than the rudder takes to move.
manoeuvring._turnSpeedLossComment: Fraction of top speed lost in a hard turn. Real ships bleed a great deal of speed heeling into a turn.
manoeuvring._shaftAsymmetryComment: Yaw rate produced per unit of port/starboard thrust imbalance, as a fraction of full-rudder yaw rate. Matters once a shaft is lost.

seakeeping._listCapsizeComment: Placeholder ceiling used before Stage 4 computes a real GZ curve; a ship past this angle is capsizing.
